/-!
# Conjecture 3.55

by S. P. Strunkov

Is every binary soluble group all of whose abelian subgroups have finite rank,
locally soluble?

Here a group is *binary soluble* if every two of its elements generate a soluble
subgroup, and *locally soluble* if every finitely generated subgroup is soluble.
The *rank* is the special rank of Prüfer and Mal'cev: a group has finite rank if
there is an $r$ such that every finitely generated subgroup can be generated by
at most $r$ elements. No finiteness assumption is made on the group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

  ∀ x y : G, IsSolvable (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

def HasFiniteSpecialRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ has *finite (special, or Prüfer–Mal'cev) rank* if there is an $r$ such
that every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ can be generated by at most $r$
elements.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Group.rank (Mathlib.GroupTheory.Rank) — requires Group.FG of the whole group, so it cannot be applied directly to arbitrary (possibly non-finitely-generated) abelian subgroups; Module.rank/finrank over ℤ (only captures torsion-free rank).
justification.name: Kourovka.«3.55».HasFiniteSpecialRank
justification.why_needed: Mathlib's Group.rank is only the minimal number of generators of a finitely generated group; there is no Prüfer/Mal'cev special rank (sup over finitely generated subgroups) nor a finiteness predicate for it. Defined as ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem HasFiniteSpecialRank.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    HasFiniteSpecialRank G := by
  classical
  refine ⟨Nat.card G, fun H _ => ?_⟩
  have := Fintype.ofFinite H
  refine (Group.rank_le (S := Finset.univ) (by simp)).trans ?_
  rw [Finset.card_univ, ← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
  exact Nat.card_le_card_of_injective (Subtype.val : H → G) Subtype.val_injective

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question: for every group G, if G is binary soluble (every 2-generator subgroup is soluble) and every abelian subgroup of G has finite (Prüfer/special) rank, is G locally soluble (every finitely generated subgroup soluble)? Formalize as answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G, ... ; note 'rank' here is the Prüfer/Mal'cev special rank (for abelian groups: finite torsion-free rank and finite p-ranks), not the minimal number of generators, and the implicit quantifier is over all groups (no finiteness assumption).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition (answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G group, binary soluble → every abelian subgroup has finite special rank → locally soluble) and all compile with only the sorry warning. c08 was chosen for style: bespoke predicates IsBinarySolvable / IsLocallySolvable / HasFiniteSpecialRank with docstrings and short fully-proved @[category API] tests (as CONTRIBUTING requests), the IsMulCommutative idiom used in Kourovka/20_76.lean, Mathlib's Group.rank for the special-rank bound, and the `G : Type` convention of the other Kourovka files (faithful, since any counterexample contains a countable f.g. non-soluble subgroup which is itself a counterexample). Used verbatim.

decomposition_objections.text: None of substance. Minor: the note's parenthetical 'for abelian groups: finite torsion-free rank and finite p-ranks' is slightly imprecise — finite special rank for an abelian group requires the p-ranks to be bounded uniformly in p, not merely finite for each p. I followed the primary designation (Prüfer/Mal'cev special rank).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.55

by S. P. Strunkov

Is every binary soluble group all of whose abelian subgroups have finite rank,
locally soluble?

Here a group is *binary soluble* if every two of its elements generate a soluble
subgroup, and *locally soluble* if every finitely generated subgroup is soluble.
The *rank* is the special rank of Prüfer and Mal'cev: a group has finite rank if
there is an $r$ such that every finitely generated subgroup can be generated by
at most $r$ elements. No finiteness assumption is made on the group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«3.55»

/-- A group $G$ is *binary soluble* if every two elements of $G$ generate a soluble
subgroup. -/
def IsBinarySolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, IsSolvable (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is *locally soluble* if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is
soluble. -/
def IsLocallySolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsSolvable H

/-- A group $G$ has *finite (special, or Prüfer–Mal'cev) rank* if there is an $r$ such
that every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ can be generated by at most $r$
elements. -/
def HasFiniteSpecialRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r

/-- A soluble group is locally soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallySolvable.of_isSolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsSolvable G] :
    IsLocallySolvable G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A locally soluble group is binary soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallySolvable.isBinarySolvable {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsLocallySolvable G) :
    IsBinarySolvable G := by
  classical
  exact fun x y => h _ ⟨{x, y}, by simp⟩

/-- A finite group has finite special rank. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem HasFiniteSpecialRank.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    HasFiniteSpecialRank G := by
  classical
  refine ⟨Nat.card G, fun H _ => ?_⟩
  have := Fintype.ofFinite H
  refine (Group.rank_le (S := Finset.univ) (by simp)).trans ?_
  rw [Finset.card_univ, ← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
  exact Nat.card_le_card_of_injective (Subtype.val : H → G) Subtype.val_injective

/--
Is every binary soluble group all of whose abelian subgroups have finite rank,
locally soluble?

That is: if every two elements of a group $G$ generate a soluble subgroup, and every
abelian subgroup of $G$ has finite special rank, is every finitely generated subgroup
of $G$ soluble?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsBinarySolvable G →
      (∀ A : Subgroup G, IsMulCommutative A → HasFiniteSpecialRank A) →
      IsLocallySolvable G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«3.55»

items: 'Finite rank' is read as finite special (Prüfer–Mal'cev) rank, as the decomposition table prescribes: there is a uniform r such that every finitely generated subgroup of the abelian subgroup is generated by ≤ r elements. For abelian groups this is equivalent to finite torsion-free rank together with p-ranks bounded uniformly in p. The table's parenthetical 'finite torsion-free rank and finite p-ranks' would, if read as 'each p-rank finite but not uniformly bounded', be a strictly weaker hypothesis (e.g. ⊕_p (ℤ/p)^p has finite p-ranks but infinite special rank); I followed the primary designation (special rank), which is the standard meaning of 'rank' in the Strunkov/Shunkov/Mal'cev literature. A reviewer should confirm this reading.

Binary soluble is formalized as: for all x y : G, the subgroup closure {x, y} is soluble (this includes 1- and 0-generator subgroups when x = y or x = y = 1, which are soluble anyway, so nothing is lost).
Locally soluble is formalized as: every finitely generated subgroup (Subgroup.FG) is IsSolvable; there is no bound on derived lengths, matching the usual definition.

Abelian subgroups are expressed as A : Subgroup G with IsMulCommutative A, following the idiom in Kourovka/20_76.lean; the rank hypothesis is applied to A as a group in its own right (its finitely generated subgroups are exactly the finitely generated subgroups of G contained in A).
The group is quantified over Type (universe 0) with no finiteness assumption, matching the convention in the other Kourovka files.

Three short @[category API] lemmas (soluble ⇒ locally soluble, locally soluble ⇒ binary soluble, finite ⇒ finite special rank) were added as basic tests of the bespoke definitions, per CONTRIBUTING.md.

reviewer_notes: Interpretation: 'binary soluble' = every two elements generate a soluble subgroup; 'locally soluble' = every finitely generated subgroup is soluble; 'rank' = special (Prüfer–Mal'cev) rank, i.e. ∃ r such that every finitely generated subgroup is generated by ≤ r elements, applied to each abelian subgroup separately (bound may depend on the subgroup). This matches the decomposition notes' primary designation and the Kargapolov/Šunkov literature the problem sits in. Several candidates (c03, c05, c06, c08) correctly objected that the notes' parenthetical gloss 'finite torsion-free rank and finite p-ranks' is imprecise: finite special rank of an abelian group requires the p-ranks to be uniformly bounded, not merely each finite (⊕_p (ℤ/p)^p is a separating example); Kurosh/Fuchs total rank r_0 + Σ r_p is a third, strictly stronger notion (⊕_p ℤ/p separates). The shipped file uses special rank. Differences among candidates were purely stylistic (inline vs. named predicates; Group.rank vs. explicit Finset generators vs. closure-of-Finset formulations, all equivalent; Type vs Type*). Verified all candidates compile; verified Group.rank, IsMulCommutative, Subgroup.FG semantics in Mathlib source. Trivial group satisfies hypotheses and conclusion, so no vacuity issue; hypotheses satisfiable by nontrivial groups (e.g. soluble groups of finite rank).
